Eliel
ĕ-lī´ĕl
n. pr. m. (Hebrew 'Eli'el, my God is God)
Hebrew 'eli, my God, doubled with 'El, God — a name that is itself a confession: my God is God. Nine or more men bear it.

Biblical Definition

Eliel means my God is God, and the men who bore it are soldiers, Levites and overseers. Among the half-tribe of Manasseh east of Jordan: “And these were the heads of the house of their fathers, even Epher, and Ishi, and Eliel, and Azriel, and Jeremiah, and Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, mighty men of valour, famous men, and heads of the house of their fathers” (1Ch 5:24). One stands in Samuel's own Levitical line, “The son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah” (1Ch 6:34). Two are named among the Benjamites of Jerusalem (1Ch 8:20, 8:22). One is a mighty man of David's: “Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai, and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam” (1Ch 11:46), and another among the Gadites who came to David at the hold, “Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh” (1Ch 12:11). And one served in Hezekiah's reform as a treasury overseer: “And Jehiel, and Azaziah, and Nahath, and Asahel, and Jerimoth, and Jozabad, and Eliel… were overseers under the hand of Cononiah” (2Ch 31:13).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) does not treat Scripture proper names; the sense is Hebrew, 'eli, my God, with 'El, God — my God is God.

expand to see more

ELIEL. A Hebrew proper name; from eli, my God, and El, God: my God is God.

OVERSEER, n. One who overlooks; a superintendent; one who has the care of.

VALOR, n. Strength of mind in regard to danger; that quality which enables a man to encounter danger with firmness; personal bravery.

Key Scripture

1Ch 5:24 — "And these were the heads of the house of their fathers, even Epher, and Ishi, and Eliel, and Azriel, and Jeremiah, and Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, mighty men of valour, famous men, and heads of the house of their fathers."

1Ch 6:34 — "The son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,"

1Ch 11:46 — "Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai, and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,"

2Ch 31:13 — "And Jehiel, and Azaziah, and Nahath, and Asahel, and Jerimoth, and Jozabad, and Eliel, and Ismachiah, and Mahath, and Benaiah, were overseers under the hand of Cononiah and Shimei his brother, at the commandment of Hezekiah the king, and Azariah the ruler of the house of God."

Modern Corruption

God is spoken of as a personal preference, while a name borne by nine ordinary Israelites insists that the God who is mine is God absolutely.

expand to see more

The name is a whole theology in two words. My God is God — the possessive and the absolute in one breath. Modern religious speech is fluent in the first half and embarrassed by the second: people will readily say what God means to them and hesitate to say what God is. Eliel refuses the split. The God who is mine is not mine because I have chosen Him; He is mine because He is God, and my claiming Him adds nothing to His being.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that Israelite parents put confessions in their children's mouths. A boy named Eliel could not introduce himself without stating a doctrine. The practice assumes what our age doubts — that faith is transmitted deliberately, through households, in the ordinary furniture of a life, and that a child is formed by what he is given to say long before he can weigh it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Eli'el (H447), my God is God; from 'el (H410), God, with the first-person suffix; the same element in Elijah, Elisha, Eliezer, Elkanah.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Eli'el (H447) — Eliel; 1 Chronicles 5:24, 6:34, 11:46, 2 Chronicles 31:13.

Hebrew 'El (H410) — God, the Mighty One; both elements of the name.

Hebrew gibbor chayil — mighty men of valour; the description in 1 Chronicles 5:24.

Hebrew paqid (H6496) — overseer; Eliel's office under Hezekiah.

Hebrew 'Eliyahu (H452) — Elijah, my God is the LORD; the same construction.

Usage

"“Mighty men of valour, famous men, and heads of the house of their fathers” — the company Eliel kept."

"“Eliel the Mahavite” — among David's mighty men."

"The name is a sentence: my God is God."
